PullRequest.Title: Attribute Agent Host first-response latency by connection kind
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Attribute the existing `agentHost.firstResponse` latency metric using the shared `AgentHostClientConnectionKind`, rather than a sandbox-specific taxonomy or configured-host lookup.

- Expose client-owned connection classification through `IAgentConnection` and capture it at invocation start in product telemetry, logs, and optional OTel diagnostics.
- Distinguish today's GitHub-managed sandboxes (`web_pub_sub`) from user-local Mission Control environments (`mission_control`), even though both use Web PubSub. Preserve all other existing connection kinds and report `unknown` when unavailable or unrecognized.
- Share the bounded validator, preserve older diagnostic payloads, and cover correlation, classification, privacy, and connection-lifecycle behavior.

No environment identities, addresses, credentials, settings, or consent paths are added. The measurement remains invocation-to-first-live-response-text latency, **not model TTFT**. The documentation includes cohort filters and makes clear that connection kind is not a permanent hosting-ownership guarantee.

## Validation

Rebased onto current `main`. Used Node 24.18.0 for npm commands.

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed after rebasing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed after rebasing.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

**Host timing and protocol suites — 225 passed after rebasing:**

```bash
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 .build/electron/code-oss ./node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/otel/agentHostTiming.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts \
  --reporter dot
```

The initial post-rebase run identified the new upstream `@hpke/core` dependency as missing; `npm run install-fast` passed, and the rerun above passed.

<details>
<summary>Additional implementation validation (unchanged telemetry implementation)</summary>

**Browser regression selection — 35 passed:**

```bash
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostFirstResponseTelemetry.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentHostTelemetry.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/services/agentHost/test/browser/editorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient.test.ts \
  --grep 'first[ -]response|AgentHostFirstResponseTiming|AgentHostTelemetry|client-owned connection kind|waits for enablement|factory recovery reuses unchanged'
```

The browser runner excludes the Electron-only protocol client file; it was covered separately below.

**Changed-TypeScript lint — 16 files passed** (run before committing):

```bash
git diff --name-only -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 npm run eslint --
```

**Native connection regressions — 2 passed using temporary bundles:**

The standard Electron invocation failed to load the large test module graph:

```bash
xvfb-run -a ./scripts/test.sh --no-sandbox --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/localAgentHostService.test.ts \
  --grep 'connection kind'
```

Bundling those same compiled test modules with the repository's existing esbuild allowed the native regressions to pass. All temporary bundles were removed.

```bash
./build/node_modules/.bin/esbuild out/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/localAgentHostService.test.js --bundle --format=esm --platform=node --packages=external --loader:.css=empty --outfile=out/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/localAgentHostService.connectionKind.bundle.test.js
./build/node_modules/.bin/esbuild out/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.js --bundle --format=esm --platform=node --packages=external --loader:.css=empty --outfile=out/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.connectionKind.bundle.test.js
xvfb-run -a ./scripts/test.sh --no-sandbox --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/localAgentHostService.connectionKind.bundle.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.connectionKind.bundle.test.ts \
  --grep 'connection kind'
```

</details>

Live cloud-provider flows and telemetry backend ingestion were not exercised.

Scenarios.Scenario: An Agent Host chat invocation starts, produces or fails to produce response text, and records renderer first-response diagnostics.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At invocation entry, the diff reads the already-created connection transport's connection-kind property and validates it against 10 constant values. This synchronous O(10) check is on the invocation path but does no I/O. At invocation completion, the existing telemetry event and log serialization include one additional bounded string; the existing best-effort host diagnostic is fire-and-forget and remains off the invocation's awaited critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the existing agentHost.firstResponse product telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per completed, cancelled, errored, or not-dispatched invocation; connection kind has effective cardinality 10 and adds one scalar field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event was submitted once per invocation without connectionKind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing publicLog2 call is synchronous at invocation finalization, but the diff only adds a constant-size string property and no additional call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the existing content-free AgentHostFirstResponse JSON log record through the log service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One log record per invocation; JSON serialization grows by one bounded key/value pair.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same record was serialized and logged without connectionKind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing JSON.stringify and log submission remain in the finally block; the diff adds constant serialization/allocation only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing vscode/reportAgentHostFirstResponse extension request to local or remote Agent Host when timing diagnostics are advertised.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one best-effort request per invocation, with no retry; one additional bounded scalar is carried in the existing payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was sent with the same frequency and scheduling without connectionKind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The caller does not await this request, so it does not delay invocation completion. Payload growth is constant.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales linearly with the existing number of Agent Host invocations, with constant additional work and bytes per invocation; it does not scale with chat history, response length, environments, tools, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each invocation creates one timing object and emits at most one of each existing diagnostic. Concurrent invocations can overlap as before; the diff introduces no limiter bypass, fan-out, retry, or extra request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated. Cold and warm behavior are identical because the classification is an in-memory transport property captured once per invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete invocation finally block and reporting implementation show unchanged emission count and scheduling, while the changed code adds only a getter read, a bounded enum validation, and one payload property.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact telemetry and logger backend costs vary by deployment, but the incremental payload is one allowlisted short string and does not alter call count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added constant CPU/allocation and bounded bytes per existing diagnostic are negligible and introduce no new expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: A client transport is created or reconnected and its connection classification is exposed through IAgentConnection.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Transport factories already create the concrete IPC, WebSocket, Web PubSub, tunnel, or remote-extension-host transport. AgentHostProtocolClient installs that transport synchronously in its constructor. The new getters only return its existing in-memory clientConnectionKind and do not connect, discover hosts, or consult configured-host state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish the existing WebSocket/Web PubSub transport connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport connection per existing connection/reconnection attempt; classification reads do not create attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same transport was created and connected; its classification already existed on IProtocolTransport but was not exposed through IAgentConnection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection establishment remains on the existing connect path; the getter does not perform network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/use the existing local or remote Agent Host IPC channel transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One channel transport per existing client lifecycle, including existing replacement semantics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC transport was created with the same connection-kind constructor value; the diff reuses that value through a property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new IPC is issued by assigning or reading clientConnectionKind.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per property read and per connection metadata validation; no dependence on repository size, sessions, or number of host resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection and reconnection concurrency is unchanged; getter reads neither schedule nor await work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The classification resides on the current transport and survives reads without lookup. Transport replacement naturally changes the backing object; there is no positive/negative cache or invalidation work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and transport code show the transport is installed before consumers can read the getter, and all expensive connection operations pre-exist.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the mechanism: property access and a 10-value linear enum check are bounded. Underlying connection latency is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This exposes existing metadata without adding connection, IPC, filesystem, or network operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: The Agent Host receives and exports an optional first-response OTel diagnostic.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing protocol request is validated on receipt. The diff validates one optional enum field and, when diagnostics are enabled, adds it to the existing synthetic span attributes before the existing exporter/store path. The server immediately resolves the request and does not flush for first-response diagnostics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive and validate the existing first-response JSON-RPC extension request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per renderer invocation when diagnostics are enabled; one bounded field is added to the same request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request and whole-object validation occurred without the connectionKind property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant validation work occurs on request handling, but no additional request or round trip is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct synthetic OTel span attributes including connectionKind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional attribute per accepted first-response diagnostic that includes the field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing span was queued with all other first-response attributes but omitted connectionKind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The extra attribute is constant-size and feeds the existing queue/export path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist/export queued OTel spans when a configured diagnostics exporter or store drains them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one synthetic span per accepted diagnostic; byte size increases by one bounded attribute with no additional write or flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same synthetic span entered the existing store/export pipeline without connectionKind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new flush is introduced, and the renderer does not await delivery. Incremental storage/export bytes are constant.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Incremental work is O(number of emitted first-response diagnostics) with a fixed 10-value validation and one bounded attribute per diagnostic.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Diagnostics retain the existing one-span-per-request behavior and existing exporter queue. The diff does not add parallel exports, flushes, retries, or bypass backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies. Diagnostics-disabled hosts reject the path before validation/export as before; enabled cold and warm exporter behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: server request handling, attribute projection, and OTel queue code directly establish unchanged call count and only one new scalar attribute.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exporter implementation and deployment frequency vary, but incremental CPU, allocation, and bytes are strictly bounded per existing span.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The serialization/allocation increase is bounded and does not create extra I/O or block the user-visible first-response path.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 17 changed files and traced invocation capture, transport exposure, protocol reporting, validation, logging, product telemetry, and OTel export. The diff adds only bounded in-memory validation and one constant-size metadata field to existing per-invocation emissions; no actionable performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was found.
